items.headline: Brachyury expression levels predict lineage potential of neuromesodermal progenitors
items.preview: Study reveals the role of Brachyury in determining the fate of neuromesodermal progenitors.
items.article:
Neuromesodermal progenitors (NMPs) are crucial for spinal cord and musculoskeletal development. This study developed a dual Sox2/Tbxt reporter mouse ESC line to investigate the functional characteristics of in vitro SOX2/TBXT co-expressing cells. 

Why this matters: Understanding the lineage potential of NMPs can enhance regenerative medicine strategies and developmental biology insights. The findings challenge existing assumptions about the regulatory roles of SOX2 and TBXT in neuromesodermal differentiation.

items.headline: Moderna vaccine, Genentech obesity deal, Trump’s FDA pick — a BioCentury podcast
items.preview: Discussion on Moderna's melanoma vaccine success and Genentech's obesity strategy.
items.article:
A Phase III melanoma win gives Moderna and Merck validation for mRNA neoantigen vaccines, raising questions about durability and scalability. Genentech's partnership with Hanmi introduces a potential first-in-class obesity treatment. 

Why this matters: These developments highlight the evolving landscape of cancer treatment and obesity management, showcasing the potential of innovative therapies in these fields.

items.headline: FDA extends review of Capricor cell therapy; Pain drug startup to go public
items.preview: Capricor's Duchenne muscular dystrophy therapy review extended by FDA.
items.article:
The FDA has extended its review of Capricor's deramiocel for Duchenne muscular dystrophy by three months due to a major amendment in the application. GSK's hepatitis B drug Hibsago received approval in Japan, and Ambros Therapeutics plans to go public through a reverse merger. 

Why this matters: These developments reflect ongoing advancements in gene therapies and the regulatory landscape for new treatments, impacting patient care and market dynamics.

items.headline: Developing a genetic toolkit for manipulating intestinal microbes
items.preview: New molecular tools developed to study Clostridia in the human gut.
items.article:
Weill Cornell Medicine researchers have created genetic tools to regulate gene activity in Clostridia, a common gut bacterium. This toolkit enables the study of how these microbes affect human health and disease. 

Why this matters: Understanding the genetic manipulation of gut bacteria could lead to breakthroughs in treating various diseases linked to microbiota, enhancing our knowledge of gut health.

items.headline: IP3R2-mediated calcium signaling suppresses melanosome degradation
items.preview: Study identifies IP3R2 as a key regulator of melanosome degradation.
items.article:
Research reveals that IP3R2 suppresses melanophagy, impacting skin pigmentation. The study utilized novel imaging probes to monitor this process and demonstrated the physiological relevance of IP3R2 in pigmentation through in vivo studies. 

Why this matters: Insights into the mechanisms of melanophagy could lead to new therapeutic targets for pigmentary disorders and skin cancers.
